title: Two-Stage and Compound Binomial Models: Inner and Outer Random Variables

questions.title: Inner Event Probability for a Multi-Day Period

parts.text: The probability that it rains on any given day is $0.15$, independently of all other days. Find the probability $q$ that at least one day in a $4$-day period has rain, giving your answer correct to 4 significant figures.

questions.title: Outer Binomial Model on Independent Time Periods

parts.text: The probability that a weekly period has a network outage is $q = 0.40$. Six independent weekly periods are observed. Find the probability that exactly 2 of the 6 weekly periods have a network outage, giving your answer correct to 4 significant figures.

questions.title: First Occurrence on a Specific Independent Trial

parts.text: An event occurs on each independent trial with probability $p = 0.12$. Find the probability that the event occurs for the first time on the 5th trial, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Coin Experiment Inner Probability and Expected Outer Count

parts.text: Three fair coins are tossed in a single trial. A trial is declared a 'Double Head' if exactly 2 heads appear. In a sequence of 8 independent trials, let $Y$ be the number of trials that are 'Double Heads'. Find $E(Y)$.

questions.title: Outer Probability of At Least One Occurrence Across Periods

parts.text: The probability that a monthly quality audit detects a compliance breach is $q = 0.28$. Across 5 independent monthly audits, find the probability that at least one audit detects a compliance breach, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Turn Distribution Table to Zero Occurrences in Repeated Turns

parts.text:
In a game, the score $X$ on a single turn has the following probability distribution:

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline x & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ \hline P(X = x) & 0.40 & a & b \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Given that $E(X) = 0.80$, find $P(X = 2)$ on a single turn, and find the probability that $X = 2$ occurs on 0 turns out of 5 independent turns.

A factory produces electronic components. The probability that an individual component is defective is $0.05$. Components are packed in boxes of $6$. Find the probability $q$ that a randomly chosen box contains at least one defective component, giving your answer correct to 4 significant figures.
Five independent boxes are inspected. Find the probability that exactly 2 of the 5 boxes contain at least one defective component, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Dice Game Threshold and Repeated Occasions

parts.text: In a game, a player rolls a fair six-sided die 4 times. The player wins the game if a six is rolled at least 2 times. Find the probability that the player wins the game, giving your answer as an exact fraction or decimal correct to 4 significant figures.
The player plays this game on 6 independent occasions. Find the probability that the player wins the game on fewer than 2 occasions, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Spin Distribution Parameters to Repeated Spin Threshold

parts.text:
In a carnival game, the number of tokens $X$ won on a single spin of a wheel has the following probability distribution:

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline x & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ \hline P(X = x) & 0.35 & a & b & 0.10 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Given that the expected number of tokens won per spin is $E(X) = 0.95$, find the values of $a$ and $b$, and hence find the probability $p$ that a player wins at least 2 tokens on a single spin.
A player spins the wheel 8 independent times. Find the probability that the player wins at least 2 tokens on at least 2 of the 8 spins, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Target Archery: First Hit and Repeated Round Success

parts.text: An archer hits the bullseye with probability $0.25$ on any independent shot. In a round of 6 shots, find the probability that the archer hits the bullseye for the first time on the 4th shot of the round, giving your answer correct to 4 significant figures.

The archer completes 5 independent rounds of 6 shots each. In any round, the archer is successful if at least one bullseye is hit. Find the probability that the archer is successful in exactly 4 of the 5 rounds, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Batch Inspection Threshold to Repeated Rejections

parts.text: A manufacturing process produces components with a defect rate of $0.08$. Components are packed into boxes of $10$. A box is rejected by quality control if it contains more than 1 defective component. Find the probability $p_{\text{rej}}$ that a randomly chosen box is rejected, giving your answer correct to 4 significant figures.
A shipment consists of 8 independent boxes. Find the probability that at least 2 boxes in the shipment are rejected, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Three-Tier Classification to Carton Composition and Sequence

parts.text: A manufacturing process produces components where each component is defective with probability $0.15$, independently of all others. Components are packed in packets of $8$. A packet is classified as 'Grade A' if it contains 0 defective components, and as 'Grade B' if it contains exactly 1 defective component. Find the probability that a packet is Grade A, and find the probability that a packet is Grade B, giving both answers correct to 4 significant figures.
A carton contains 6 packets. Find the probability that a carton contains at least 3 Grade A packets, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

Cartons are dispatched one after another. A carton is called 'Premium' if it contains at least 3 Grade A packets. Find the probability that the first Premium carton dispatched is either the 2nd carton or the 3rd carton dispatched, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Two-Stage Sampling Acceptance Plan to Repeated Delivery Lots

parts.text:
In a quality assurance scheme, large batches of components are inspected using a two-stage sampling plan. The defect probability for any component is $0.10$, independently of all others.
- A first sample of $5$ components is tested ($X_1 \sim B(5, 0.10)$).
- If $X_1 = 0$, the batch is accepted immediately.
- If $X_1 \ge 2$, the batch is rejected immediately.
- If $X_1 = 1$, a second sample of $5$ components is tested ($X_2 \sim B(5, 0.10)$). The batch is accepted if and only if $X_2 = 0$.

Find the probability $p_{\text{acc}}$ that a randomly chosen batch is accepted, giving your answer correct to 4 significant figures.
Six independent batches are tested using this two-stage plan. Find the probability that exactly 5 batches are accepted, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

In a continuous audit, batches are tested one by one until a batch is rejected. Find the probability that the first rejected batch occurs on the 4th batch tested, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
